# Draft:Canadian Forces Electronic Warfare Centre

----
Canadian Forces Electronic Warfare Centre
Canadian Forces Electronic Warfare Cantre, also known as CFEWC, is a Canadian Forces unit located at the Shirley's Bay Campus in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. A unit with the Canadian Armed Forces Cyber Command, it is tasked to produced electromagnetic intelligence and intelligence mission data as an integral capability to CAF operations. The unit's motto is MENS ET MEMORIA, which is a latin phrase which means "Intellect and Recollection". CFS Leitrim is the sister unit of CFEWC.
CFEWC was official stood up on 8 March 1996.
History
The Canadian Forces Electronic Warfare Centre (CFEWC) was formerly known as the Electronic Warfare Emitter Data Centre (EWEDC). Prior to 1990, this organization operated out of the Tilley Building. That year, the unit relocated to the Billings Bridge Tower, later moving to the Shirley’s Bay campus of the Communications Research Centre in Ottawa’s west end, where it remains today. In 1994, it was redesignated as the Interim Electronic Warfare Operational Support Centre (IEWOSC). At that time, the unit consisted of approximately 35 personnel and was based in Building T5 at the Shirley’s Bay complex.
The Electronic Warfare Operational Support Centre (EWOSC) project was launched in 1990 with the goal of bringing together operational, intelligence, and engineering support for the Canadian Forces electronic warfare community. The project was designed as a long-term initiative that would enable a smooth and efficient transition of both existing and future EW capabilities into a centralized, national-level organization. The initial stage of this effort was known as the Interim EWOSC, which focused on establishing the foundational structure required for subsequent development.
Under the IEWOSC, several key capabilities were put in place. These included the creation of a centralized Canadian Forces electronic warfare database, the establishment of integrated environmental support stations (Naval Electronic Warfare Centre, A3 Electronic Warfare Operational Support, and LISS), the initiation of EW threat analysis activities, and the formation of a unified logistics and administrative support function. These combined capabilities led to the formal establishment of the Canadian Forces Electronic Warfare Centre, supported by purpose-built facilities at the Communications Research Centre’s Shirley’s Bay campus. Construction of these facilities was completed in 1994.
As part of its responsibilities under the IEWOSC framework, CFEWC was tasked with developing the Canadian Forces Electronic Warfare Database (CFEWDB). This relational database serves as a comprehensive, single-source reference for the Canadian Forces, containing detailed information such as emitter characteristics, platform associations, and weapon system integrations. Ongoing development of the database aims to expand its scope to include electro-optical and infrared signature data in the future.
In 2014, the COHO project was launched to deliver software-based solutions for the Canadian Forces Electronic Warfare Centre (CFEWC) at Shirley’s Bay in Ottawa. The project’s objective was to supply systems integration, system and software design, and software development services. Through this work, the project was to support CFEWC in strengthening and advancing the electronic warfare capabilities of the Canadian Armed Forces.
In 2025, it hosted the 95th NATO Emitter Database Advisory Group.
